title: The Tripitika
speaker: Kanho Chris Burkhart
summary: Kanho Chris Burkhart's talk highlights the interconnectedness of pain and joy in life, using personal experiences as a catalyst to explore the Buddhist concept of the Tripitaka, or Three Baskets. Specifically, they will delve into the Vinaya basket, which contains the monastic code governing behavior for monks and nuns, created over 2500 years ago to promote fairness, accountability, and community harmony in daily life within the sangha.

So now I will describe each of the three baskets briefly before going into more detail on the Vinaya Pitaka.
The Vinaya Pitaka is usually listed first, and that basket contains the monastic rules and guidelines for the Sangha, the Buddhist monastic community at the time.
Lay Buddhist communities such as ours did not really exist.

The job of the lay practitioners was to support the monks and to hope that in a future lifetime they also would be reborn as monks, because that was determined to be the best way of reaching enlightenment.
So the Vinaya Pitaka provides a framework for ethical conduct, outlining the path towards discipline, harmony and communal living.
Through its rules and precepts, the Vinaya Pitaka embodies the importance of cultivating virtues and harmonious relationships in spiritual practice.
The next basket is the one we are so familiar with.
That is the Sutta Pitaka.

This basket contains the discourses delivered by the Gautama Buddha, and they also include longer stories as captured in the, you have guessed it, the long discourses of the Buddha, like the Buddha's last days and so on.

Abhidharma is Sanskrit and Abhidhamma is Pali.
It's often described as Buddhist psychology and regarded as the philosophical core of Buddhist thought.
It explores the intricate workings of the mind, consciousness, and the nature of reality through analytical and systematic teachings.

Our practice does not deal with the Abhidharma very much, even though it's really interesting, because it's too technical, an abstract, highly technical system of Buddhist doctrine.
